newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL MADRID STALWART SAPORTA DIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL MADRID STALWART SAPORTA DIES.

text.p: Raimundo Saporta, the man who brought Alfredo di Stefano to Real Madrid in the 1950s and who organised the 1982 World Cup finals in Spain, died from a kidney infection on Sunday. He was 70.
Saporta, who was also a vice-president of basketball's governing body FIBA, joined the Madrid club as an administrator in the 1950s.
He helped chairman Santiago Bernabeu create a side that won the European Cup six times.
"After Bernabeu he was the most important man for Real Madrid," said current Real chairman Lorenzo Sanz.
Saporta's funeral was held on Monday.
